{
  "research_question": "Do mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion) differ across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as factor, but assess normality and homoscedasticity given extreme max value (201.39) suggesting right skew; consider log transformation or Welch's ANOVA if variance heterogeneity present",
    "For Success: One-way ANOVA is inappropriate because Success is binary (0/1); use logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as categorical predictor or chi-square test of independence; if ANOVA insisted upon, note violation of normality and use Kruskal-Wallis as nonparametric alternative",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm, but assess normality due to extreme max (29.82) and right-skewed distribution; consider robust ANOVA or transformation",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm, assess normality given max 75.35 vs mean 12.50; likely right-skewed requiring transformation or robust methods",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm; bounded [0,1] variable with mean 0.38, sd 0.24; assess normality but likely acceptable for ANOVA; consider beta regression as alternative given bounded support"
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assume satisfied given experimental design with 76,655 observations across 8 mice; verify no mouse-level clustering violates independence",
    "Normality: Shapiro-Wilk or Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests on residuals for each response; Q-Q plots essential given extreme max values in Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, and Average Speed",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's or Bartlett's test for equal variances across 5 paradigms; likely violated given Sham mean Time-to-Target (4.68) vs Combined (2.56) with similar SDs but different ranges",
    "Sample size balance: Severe imbalance—Combined (48,846) vs Sham (3,505); Welch's ANOVA or weighted methods may be needed",
    "For Success: Binomial assumption violated for ANOVA; use appropriate GLM instead"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA significant for Time-to-Target: Games-Howell post-hoc (unequal variances and sample sizes) or Tukey HSD with Welch correction; focus on Sham vs active stimulation paradigms given large mean difference (Sham 4.68s vs Combined 2.56s)",
    "If logistic regression used for Success: Estimated marginal means with pairwise comparisons using z-tests; focus on Sham (27.3% success) vs Combined (78.0%), Bright Visual (78.5%), ICMS Only (68.5%), Dim Visual (67.3%)",
    "If ANOVA significant for Path Efficiency: Games-Howell or Tukey HSD; Sham (0.308) substantially lower than all active paradigms (~0.43-0.50)",
    "If ANOVA significant for Average Speed: Games-Howell; Sham (10.74) slower than Combined (12.83), Bright Visual (12.68), ICMS Only (12.04), Dim Visual (11.97)",
    "If ANOVA significant for AD: Tukey HSD or Games-Howell; Sham (0.236) lower than all active paradigms (~0.34-0.40), suggesting more directed movement with stimulation",
    "Apply Bonferroni or FDR correction for multiple comparisons across 10 pairwise tests per response variable"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham paradigm shows markedly impaired performance: highest Time-to-Target (4.68s vs ~2.6-3.1s), lowest Success rate (27.3% vs 67-79%), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308 vs 0.43-0.50), slowest Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lowest AD (0.236 vs 0.34-0.40)",
    "Combined and Bright Visual Only paradigms appear numerically superior on most metrics, though formal inference needed",
    "Dim Visual Only and ICMS Only show intermediate performance, closer to Combined than to Sham",
    "Success rates suggest ceiling effects for Combined and Bright Visual (~78-79%) vs floor effect for Sham (27%)",
    "AD pattern suggests stimulation increases path tortuosity or exploration (higher angular dispersion), except Sham which shows more directed paths"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe sample size imbalance: Combined has 14× more observations than Sham, reducing power for Sham comparisons and potentially inflating Type I error for unequal variance tests",
    "Mouse-level clustering ignored: 8 mice with unequal observations (7,233-10,986 per mouse); mixed-effects models would better account for non-independence",
    "Success as binary variable makes ANOVA inappropriate; analysis plan must use logistic regression or nonparametric alternative",
    "Extreme outliers in Time-to-Target (max 201s), Path Efficiency (max 29.8), and Average Speed (max 75.4) suggest heavy-tailed distributions requiring transformation or robust methods",
    "No information on trial-level structure, learning effects, or temporal dependencies; repeated-measures structure unaccounted for",
    "Single replication (Run ID 14, Replication 1) limits generalizability; no estimate of run-to-run variability"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) with Mouse as random effect for Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and AD; use logistic mixed-effects model for Success; include Stim Paradigm as fixed effect with sum or treatment contrasts (reference=Sham); use Kenward-Roger or Satterthwaite df approximation; if LMMs fail to converge, use generalized estimating equations (GEE) with robust standard errors; report estimated marginal means with 95% CIs and pairwise comparisons with Holm-Bonferroni adjustment; visualize paradigm effects with boxplots showing raw data distribution given extreme outliers"
}
